annotations.description: Playing the land before casting Badgermole Cub means the Chocobo gets a +1/+1 counter from the land's landfall trigger, but Badgermole Cub's earthbend ability (which animates a land and puts a +1/+1 counter on it) would also trigger landfall if sequenced differently. More importantly, casting Badgermole Cub first (with the 2 forests already available) and then playing the land would trigger landfall on both Sazh's Chocobo AND the earthbent land creature (if it counts as entering). However, the key issue is that playing the Forest first is actually fine for Chocobo, but casting Badgermole Cub before the land drop would let you earthbend the newly played Forest after it enters untapped (since you'd play it post-Cub). Actually, with 2 Forests untapped, casting Badgermole Cub first uses both forests, then playing the 3rd Forest gives landfall to Chocobo. Playing Forest first gives landfall to Chocobo, then casting Cub with 2 of 3 forests uses mana but earthbends a land. The sequencing matters because playing the land first and then casting Badgermole Cub means the Cub's earthbend targets one of 3 forests. If instead they cast Cub first (2 forests, both tapped), then play Forest (landfall on Chocobo), the earthbend from Cub still targets one of the 2 tapped forests. The land-first line is slightly better since it gives an extra untapped forest as an earthbend target, but the real consideration is whether Mossborn Hydra at 3 mana (with the 3rd forest) would have been better than Badgermole Cub - Mossborn Hydra enters as 1/1 with trample, and subsequent land drops double its counters, which could be very powerful. But Badgermole Cub at 2 mana plus land drop is reasonable. The sequencing of land before creature is slightly suboptimal in that it telegraphs information, but functionally the play is acceptable.

This would provide immediate board presence comparable to the Hydra (two 1/1s vs one 1/1), plus ramp for next turn to cast Icetill Explorer, and start accumulating quest counters for the landfall trigger. The Mossborn Hydra enters as a 1/1 with trample, and while its landfall ability to double counters is powerful, Earthbender Ascension sets up the mana base and board state more effectively at this stage. Additionally, playing Earthbender Ascension first means future land drops (including from Icetill Explorer next turn) would trigger both the Ascension's quest counters and the Hydra's counter-doubling when the Hydra is cast later with more lands available.
